meta.title: Firmware unit tests on the host (with mutation testing)
meta.tools: Minimal C test framework, host-compiled embedded modules (ring buffer, CRC-16, Q15 math), mutation testing driver in Python
meta.summary: Test three embedded modules on the PC with a tiny assertion framework, measure line coverage with clang's instrumentation, then deliberately inject bugs (mutants) and count how many the tests catch.
meta.problem: Firmware bugs are expensive to find on hardware. How much of an embedded module can be verified on a PC, and how do you know the tests are any good?
meta.theory:
Code coverage measures what the tests execute; mutation score measures what they would *notice*. A good suite should kill ≥ 90 % of simple
mutants (off-by-one, flipped comparison, wrong constant). Surviving mutants point at untested behaviour, not just unexecuted lines.
meta.method:
Modules: ring buffer (push/pop/full/empty/wrap), CRC-16/CCITT (check value 0x29B1 for "123456789"), Q15 saturating multiply. 14 tests. Coverage via
-fprofile-instr-generate/llvm-cov if available (else line-execution counting). 12 hand-written mutants compiled and run one by one.

rows.quantity: Tests failing on the correct code
